question.prompt:
In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AC=CD\) and \(\angle CAB-\angle ABC=30^\circ.\) Then \(\angle BAD\) is:

[Figure 1](figures/1957_AMC_12_Q44_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The equality \(AC=CD\) makes triangle \(ACD\) isosceles, so its angles at \(A\) and \(D\) are equal. This lets us connect the requested angle to the given angle difference.

As shown, \(D\) lies between \(C\) and \(B\). Let \(x=\angle BAD\) and \(b=\angle ABC=\angle ABD\). In triangle \(ABD\), \(\angle ADC\) is an exterior angle, so
\[
\angle ADC=x+b.
\]
Since \(AC=CD\), we also have \(\angle CAD=x+b\). Adding the two parts of the angle at \(A\) gives
\[
\angle CAB=x+(x+b)=2x+b.
\]
Therefore the given difference becomes \(2x=30^\circ\), so \(\angle BAD=15^\circ\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Equal base angles and an exterior angle
